subtitle: Names in Stone: The Sculptors of the Hoysalas

panels.shot: epic low-angle of a star-shaped Hoysala temple wall with a tiny sculptor’s name carved near a riot of stone detail
panels.action: Ruvari Mallitamma kneels beside a richly carved Hoysala temple frieze, chisel poised near a small, half-finished name on the stone, as the intricate star-shaped temple spreads behind him under a bright sky.

dialogue.text: In an age when most temples hid their makers, the Hoysalas let sculptors like Ruvari Mallitamma, Dasoja and Chavana carve their names into living stone—and history has not forgotten.

i18n.hi: जब ज़्यादातर मंदिर अपने कारीगरों को छुपाते थे, होयसला राज में रुवारी मल्लितम्मा, दसोजा और चवना जैसे शिल्पकार ज़िंदा पत्थर पर अपना नाम उकेरते थे — और इतिहास ने उन्हें याद रखा।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Halebidu’s temple complex in partial ruin with surrounding fields and village
panels.action: The ruined yet majestic Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu stands amid green fields and quiet village houses, its star-shaped platform and dense carvings glowing in the soft late afternoon light.

dialogue.text: Centuries after the Hoysalas fell, Halebidu lies quiet. Stone elephants, warriors, dancers still cling to the ruined walls, their lines sharp, their makers mostly silent.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, होयसला राज मिट चुका है, हालेबीडू शांत है। पत्थर के हाथी, योद्धा, नर्तक खंडहर दीवारों से चिपके हैं, रेखाएँ तीखी हैं, उनके बनाने वाले ज़्यादातर ख़ामोश।

panels.shot: slow push-in along the temple wall focusing on friezes, then a tiny inscription band
panels.action: The viewpoint glides along a carved frieze of warriors and scrollwork, then stops at a narrow band of Kannada letters carved neatly between ornamental patterns on the temple base.

dialogue.text: But at Halebidu, Belur and other Hoysala shrines, small lines of Kannada script cut across the silence, naming sculptors in the very walls they carved.

i18n.hi: पर हालेबीडू, बेलूर और दूसरे होयसला मंदिरों में, कन्नड़ लिपि की पतली पंक्तियाँ इस सन्नाटे को चीरती हैं, दीवारों पर ही उन शिल्पकारों के नाम लिखती हैं जिन्होंने उन्हें तराशा।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of inscription letters on weathered stone
panels.action: An extreme close-up reveals weathered but legible Kannada characters, their grooves catching sunlight on an aged stone block of a temple base.

dialogue.text: Epigraphia Carnatica records them carefully: Ruvari Mallitamma. Dasoja. Chavana. Malloja. Names of hands that shaped this stone eight centuries ago.

i18n.hi: एपिग्राफ़िया कार्नाटिका उन्हें सहेज कर दर्ज करती है: रुवारी मल्लितम्मा। दसोजा। चवना। मल्लोजा। आठ सौ साल पहले इस पत्थर को आकार देने वाले हाथों के नाम।

panels.shot: interior workshop-wide shot, busy sculptor’s yard near a temple under construction
panels.action: In a bustling twelfth-century sculptors’ yard beside a half-built star-shaped temple, Ruvari Mallitamma, Dasoja and Chavana stand among apprentices, stone blocks, and partly carved panels, tools laid out on the ground.

dialogue.text: Travel back to the twelfth and thirteenth centuries: the Hoysala realm in southern Karnataka, where royal ambition and skilled workshops turned hard chloritic schist into forests of sculpture.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं–तेरहवीं शताब्दी में लौटो: दक्षिण कर्नाटक में होयसला शासन, जहाँ शाही महत्वाकांक्षा और निपुण कार्यशालाओं ने सख़्त पत्थर को मूर्तियों के जंगल में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: medium group shot, sculptors conferring over a design sketch on palm leaf
panels.action: Ruvari Mallitamma unrolls a palm-leaf sketch while Dasoja and Chavana lean in, studying the planned arrangement of friezes and bracket figures for a temple wall, apprentices watching eagerly.

dialogue.text: Kings and queens commissioned grand temples. But it was organized workshops—masters like Ruvari Mallitamma, Dasoja and Chavana—who planned, divided and executed this avalanche of detail.

i18n.hi: राजा–रानी भव्य मंदिर बनवाते थे। पर यही संगठित कार्यशालाएँ — रुवारी मल्लितम्मा, दसोजा, चवना जैसे उस्ताद — इस बारीक़ी की आँधी को योजना, बाँट और अंजाम तक पहुँचाते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Mallitamma carving, dust flying, temple behind
panels.action: Ruvari Mallitamma, focused and steady, strikes his chisel against a stone slab, fine dust rising as the beginnings of a dancing figure emerge, the temple’s star-shaped platform looming behind.

dialogue.text: In much of India, temple art remained anonymous. Here, the sculptors were visible, standing at the center of royal projects, their status high enough for their names to be preserved.

i18n.hi: भारत के ज़्यादातर हिस्सों में मंदिर कला बेनाम रही। यहाँ शिल्पकार दिखते हैं, राज–परियोजनाओं के केंद्र में खड़े, इतना मान–सम्मान कि उनके नाम बच कर रह गए।

panels.shot: workshop interior, close three-quarter shot of the three discussing layout on a temple base
panels.action: The three craftsmen crouch by the temple base, tracing sections with charcoal, marking where epics, animals and ornamental bands will run, with an overseer from the royal side watching in approval.

dialogue.text: They did not simply follow orders. Inscriptions and patterns of style show them planning entire runs of friezes, directing teams, shaping how stories would live on stone.

i18n.hi: वे बस हुक्म नहीं मानते थे। शिलालेख और शैली की लकीरें दिखाती हैं कि वे पूरे फ्रीज़ की योजना करते, टोली चलाते, कहानियों को पत्थर पर जीने का रूप तय करते थे।

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of Dasoja gesturing toward bracket figures while Chavana inspects a finished piece
panels.action: Dasoja points towards a row of elaborate bracket figures and ornamental panels stacked against a wall, while Chavana runs his hand over the smooth, polished surface of a completed relief, testing its finish.

dialogue.speaker: ruvari_mallitamma_dasoja_and_chavana
dialogue.text: Each hand leaves a pattern. Our stone must speak for us.

i18n.hi: हर हाथ अपनी पहचान छोड़ता है। हमारा पत्थर ही हमारी आवाज़ है।

panels.shot: close-up on Mallitamma’s thoughtful face, temple wall blurred behind
panels.action: Ruvari Mallitamma looks up from his work, eyes measuring the long temple wall where blocks are being hauled into place, half-carved panels already set in a rising sequence.

dialogue.text: Yet even here, not every panel can be tied to a name. Styles suggest authorship, but unless an inscription names a sculptor beside a work, attribution remains careful, sometimes uncertain.

i18n.hi: फिर भी यहाँ भी हर पैनल किसी नाम से नहीं जुड़ता। शैली लेखकों का अंदाज़ देती है, पर जब तक शिलालेख किसी मूर्ति के पास शिल्पकार का नाम न दे, पहचान सावधान, कभी–कभी अनिश्चित रहती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Chavana carving a small inscription band below a relief
panels.action: Chavana bends close beneath a narrative relief, carefully incising a neat band of Kannada letters along the base of the stone, his chisel strokes precise and deliberate.

dialogue.text: Where their names do appear, they sit in small bands of script. Sometimes a simple statement that this piece is by so-and-so, sometimes a modest phrase linking artist, patron and deity.

i18n.hi: जहाँ उनके नाम दिखते हैं, वे छोटी–सी लिपि की पट्टियों में बैठे होते हैं। कभी सीधी सूचना कि यह काम फलाँ का है, कभी विनम्र पंक्ति जो कलाकार, संरक्षक और देवता को जोड़ती है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot showing a patron or temple official observing as Mallitamma signs
panels.action: Ruvari Mallitamma kneels to carve his name on a finished block while a temple official in fine garments watches, arms folded, the rising tower and scaffolded walls framing them.

dialogue.text: The very fact that these signatures exist tells us something: sculptors were respected. Their prestige high enough that royal and temple administrations allowed, even valued, a maker’s mark.

i18n.hi: इन दस्तख़तों का होना ही बहुत कुछ कहता है: शिल्पकारों को सम्मान था। उनकी प्रतिष्ठा इतनी कि राज और मंदिर प्रशासन ने उनकी निशानी को न सिर्फ़ मंज़ूर, बल्कि क़द्र दी।

panels.shot: modern scholarly scene, wide shot of S. Settar-like scholar recording inscription
panels.action: A modern researcher with notebook and camera crouches by a Hoysala temple base in bright daylight, copying the inscription letters while the ancient carvings loom around him.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars like S. Settar trace these small lines, building maps of workshops and styles. Names in stone become evidence, showing how artistic labor was organized eight hundred years ago.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान जैसे एस. सेत्तार इन तुकड़ों का पीछा करते हैं, कार्यशालाओं और शैलियों के नक़्शे बनाते हैं। पत्थर में नाम सबूत बन जाते हैं, दिखाते हैं कि आठ सौ साल पहले कला–श्रम कैसे संगठित था।

panels.shot: institutional wide shot, UNESCO-style evaluators walking around temple ensemble
panels.action: A group of conservation experts and officials in contemporary attire walk around the temple ensemble, pointing to carvings and noting details, the temple framed with scaffolding and protective fencing.

dialogue.text: When UNESCO recognized the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas in 2023, it highlighted these very signatures as proof of artistic agency and prestigious standing within temple projects.

i18n.hi: जब यूनेस्को ने 2023 में होयसला के पवित्र मंदिर–समूहों को मान्यता दी, तो इन्हीं दस्तख़तों को कलाकार की भूमिका और मंदिर परियोजनाओं में उनकी प्रतिष्ठा का साक्ष्य माना।

panels.shot: time-crossing montage shot, translucent figures of the sculptors over today’s temple
panels.action: Ghostly, translucent forms of Ruvari Mallitamma, Dasoja and Chavana appear over the present-day temple, as tourists walk below the carvings, unaware of the hands that once shaped them.

dialogue.text: Their world has vanished—royal courts, workshop commands, the clang of chisels on fresh stone. But their names bridge that distance, tying human lives to enduring form.

i18n.hi: उनकी दुनिया जा चुकी है — राजदरबार, कार्यशाला के हुक्म, ताज़ा पत्थर पर छेनी की टन–टन। पर उनके नाम वह दूरी पाटते हैं, इंसानी ज़िंदगी को टिकाऊ रूप से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of an un-signed panel next to a signed inscription band
panels.action: A richly carved panel without visible inscription sits beside another block bearing a small, legible sculptor-name band, both catching the same slant of sunlight.

dialogue.text: The Hoysalas were not alone in allowing artists to sign. But here, the sheer number and clarity of signatures make this landscape unusually rich in documented, individual makers.

i18n.hi: होयसला कलाकारों को दस्तख़त देने में अकेले नहीं थे। पर यहाँ नामों की संख्या और स्पष्टता इस धरती को दर्ज, व्यक्तिगत कारीगरों से भरी एक अनोखी जगह बना देती है।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of Mallitamma’s hand carving the last stroke of his name
panels.action: Ruvari Mallitamma’s hand presses the chisel for a final stroke, completing his name on the stone; his other hand steadies the block, the carved letters crisp and fresh.

dialogue.speaker: ruvari_mallitamma_dasoja_and_chavana
dialogue.text: The temple is for the god. The name is for memory.

i18n.hi: मंदिर देवता के लिए है। नाम याद के लिए।

panels.shot: concluding wide shot of the Hoysala temple at sunset, carvings glowing
panels.action: The Hoysala temple stands bathed in warm sunset light, its star-shaped plan and dense carvings glowing softly, the tiny inscription bands barely visible along the base.

dialogue.text: Today we admire the stone and the stories. Their signatures remind us that behind every masterpiece stood real craftsmen whose honored names carved them a place in history’s memory.

i18n.hi: आज हम पत्थर और कहानियों की प्रशंसा करते हैं। उनके दस्तख़त याद दिलाते हैं कि हर शाहकार के पीछे असली कारीगर थे, जिनके सम्मानित नामों ने उन्हें इतिहास की याद में जगह तराश दी।

subtitle_i18n.en: Names in Stone: The Sculptors of the Hoysalas
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर पर नाम: होयसला के शिल्पकार
